title: Investigation continues into death of Vancouver man after Tasering
subtitle: B.C.'s Independent Investigations Office is continuing its investigation into whether the Tasering of Vancouver resident Alton Bernard Cuyugan, 33, by police Tuesday had any role in his death.
article: B.C.'s Independent Investigations Office is continuing its investigation into whether the Tasering of Vancouver resident Alton Bernard Cuyugan, 33, by police Tuesday had any role in his death.
The IIO said Cuyugan was jolted by a Taser after police responded to a report in the 1300-block of Renfrew of an agitated man armed with a knife who was threatening to hurt himself.
Police moved to arrest him and as Cuyugan was hit by the Taser he is believed to have injured himself with the knife, according to the BC Coroners Service.

He was taken to hospital, but died, and two teams of IIO investigators are examining the incident. IIO spokesman Owen Court said the investigation is still in its early stages and he didn't know the extent of the man's injuries before his death.
"That's something our investigators will look at in the sequence of events," Court said. "We'll certainly be investigating whether the actions of the officers contributed to his death.
"At this point we don't know the cause of death," added Court.

The BC Coroners Service is also investigating. After the IIO determines whether any criminal charges should be laid against the police officers who arrested Cuyugan the coroners service will make any recommendations that could have prevented his death.
This could involve things like police training or any treatment Cuyugan received for any possible mental health issues, spokeswoman Barb McClintock said.
